thread:
Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak in canary, we're seeing a small but consistent reg on short prefill latencies (50-120ms added on p95).
Priya: Ugh. Where is the extra time coming from? kernel decision overhead or queuing? :thinking:
Alex: Profiled one trace — decision time up ~10ms for many requests, but most of the delta is queueing in the prefill prioritizer when decode inflight tasks are hairy.
Mateo: Can you paste the lightweight flame? curious about CPU vs GPU stalls.
Alex: Sure — here's the short snippet from perf-top (simplified):
```
kernel_selector_decide()  12.4%  user
prefill_queue_wait()     29.1%  wait
kv_warmup_check()        5.3%   sys
gpu_dispatch             42.0%  gpu
```
Linh: That prefill_queue_wait jump smells like contention with decode lanes. Are prefill/decode using the same token-budget tokenslice right now?
Alex: Yes. Current heuristic shares a single token_budget target per-gpu and splits by weight. When decode storms happen, prefill gets pushed back.
Gabe: Proposed quick fix: separate the token_budget into phase buckets (prefill_budget, decode_budget) and enforce soft minima for prefill so short requests don't sit. Also consider fastpath kernel selection for tiny seq-len prefill.
Priya: Sounds reasonable. Do we have numbers for how much prefill latency reduces if we carve 20% baseline for prefill?
Mateo: Ran a sim with our workload replay: p95 prefill latency down ~38% when prefill_min=0.2, overall throughput drop <2%.
Alex: Nice. Any regressor risk? kernel fallback diversity increases when we force prefill fastpath — might hit quantized kernel degens.
Linh: We should add a quick canary: add config flags:
```
runtime.prefill_min_fraction = 0.2
runtime.kernel_fastpath_min_seq = 8
runtime.phase_affinity = "soft"
```
and measure p95+p99 for both phases separately.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued — canary group: eng-runtime-canary-3 (image: gcr/redwood/runtime:canary-20260318)
Gabe: If canary looks good, follow with a kernel-selector optimization: memoize decision per (model, seq_bucket, dtype) for 500ms to avoid repeated decisions on high QPS.
Priya: Memoization probably safe but add invalidation when we switch quantization profile or device affinity.
Alex: Agreed. I'll open a small RFC with the sim plots and perf traces. Plan: canary with prefill_min_fraction=0.2 + fastpath kernel for seq<=8 + memoization disabled initially. If good, enable memoization and phase-affinity soft enforcement.
Mateo: Also add a KV-cache warmup probe — sometimes prefill waits for kv_warmup_check to return; we can make that async for prefill.
Linh: Good call. Async KV warmup for prefill should shave a few ms.
Priya: Thanks team. Alex, please tag me on the RFC. If canary fails, rollback to previous kernel-selector and we'll iterate.
Alex: Will do. Posting results in this thread after the canary runs (~30m). :rocket:
